texts.title: Universe A5-01
texts.summary: How the universe began, how its will called Balance keeps the galaxies in check, and how Planet Dawnbreak and Planet Oro were born.

blocks.x: Universe's Origin

In the beginning, there is nothing but a chaotic energy singularity, until one day, the Big Bang happens and the embryo of Universe A5-01 emerges. After zillions of years of inflation, Universe A5-01 reaches a relatively stable condition and begins to thrive under the guidance of "Balance" - the Will of the Cosmos.
Will of the Cosmos

Universe A5-01 has its own consciousness "Balance" from the very beginning of the Big Bang. But not all galaxies within it have a will of their own. The themes of the galaxies' wills are not exactly the same. To some galaxies, killing is everything, while some other ones hold a more peaceful idea such as surviving and thriving. But all in all, they all are checked and balanced by the Will of the Cosmos. Galaxy A-19 is relatively young galaxy in the cosmos but it is one of the galaxies that hold the same "balance" idea with the universe. A-19 and its fellow galaxies are called the "Enforcers", they believe they are destined to keep the universe balanced on behalf of the universe. In A-19, there is a planet called Dawnbreak, it forms its will 2.6 billion years after its birth.
Birth of the Planet
Planet Dawnbreak

Planet Dawnbreak is a planet in Universe A5-01. It was born in the Galaxy A-19 of the Saintess Constellation billions of years ago. In its early ages, it is full of nitrogen and its surface diurnal temperature variation is extreme, no life form can survive. Eons of asteroid and meteor impact greatly enrich the resources on the planet and bring plankton to the world. The planktons change the structure of the atmosphere bit by bit and after billions of years, all kinds of lifeforms emerge.
Planet Oro

Planet Oro is a planet in Universe A5-01. It was born in the Galaxy A-20 of the Aquila Constellation billions of years ago. The will of A-20 is "Balance", the same as the universe. It was a nitrogen gas planet in its early years. After billions of years of microbial action, it is now habitable planet.

The only academy that cultivates Aspirants in Terrinia. Its Elite Educational philosophy only allows children around 14 years old with an outstanding force of faith to enter its preparatory course for cultivation.
The Council
A venue for the three powers, Decisionmakers, the Institute of Technology, and the Beau Monde, to hold important meetings or pep rallies about Androids.
Training Field
A training venue exclusive for Androids to improve their combat capability.
Energy System
A landmark building in Terrinia that provides energy for the Defensive Bubble. It enwraps the whole city to resist the Ender's invasions.

texts.title: Places
texts.summary: A short guide to the Storm Citadel, Terrinia, Selrick Academy and the Aspirants, under the motto of the blade that severs despair.

blocks.x: Blade of Aspirant Power, Sever Despair!

Powerful invaders known as "The Enders" have descended upon Planet Dawnbreak, launching an attack on humanity. The heavy burden of saving the world now falls upon the shoulders of the young warriors who pilot mecha driven by humanity's hope. Only their bonds can carry them through the depths of despair, letting their hopes resonate and shine as one!.
Storm Citadel

The Storm Citadel is a colossal Enders mothership, sent to crush humanity's resistance once and for all. Concealed within storm clouds, it can unleash devastating electromagnetic interference over large areas.
Terrinia

To fight back against destruction, humanity reverse-engineered the wreckage of The Enders, developing mecha driven by humanity's hope and training the "Aspirants" capable of facing The Ender's head-on. Terrinia became humanity's final bastion.
Selrick Academy
Within the city stands Selrick Academy, a place where young warriors are trained to pilot these miracle mecha. They are humanity's sharpest blade, and its last hope.
Aspirants
The Aspirants are gifted individuals trained to defend humanity from The Enders. They pilot advanced mecha using Aspirant power to safeguard the last human cities and ultimately reclaim their planet.

texts.title: Entities
texts.summary: The Androids, the Enders, Joe, Ruby's father, the droids, the trainee divisions, Oro's soldiers and Tetra, in a line or two each.

blocks.x: Androids
Androids nicknamed "Cosmic Reapers" were born by Project "Angel".
The Enders

When a planet with the Will of Balance finds that the existence of a certain population is prosperous enough to endanger the survival of others, it will send the Enders to wreak havoc on it with the aim to achieve balance. The Enders, who usually appear near the target population, have a solid metal shell and expose their weak spots only when they launch attacks. The Enders don't strike easily. They represent the Will of the Planet, which enters a coma once the Enders are damaged. The Enders are classified into three ranks: Ultimate Enders, Super Enders, and Enders. Ultimate Enders can release Super Enders and Enders, which though not as lethal as the Ultimate Enders, are the main killing forces due to their large number.
Joe
A Combat Division instructor of Selrick Academy. The exclusive instructor of the Layla-Fanny Team.
Ruby's Father
As the leader of Decisionmakers, he is very strict with Ruby.
AI Droids
Intelligent robots that can be seen everywhere in the Academy.
Support Division Trainee

Children who fail the entrance assessment will enter the Support Division. After one year's preparatory course, they will be divided into support teams in pairs, each for a certain Aspirant. The specialities of a support team's two members respectively lie in mecha repair and psychiatry repair.
Combat Division Trainee

Children who have passed the entrance assessment are eligible to take the Academy's introductory assessment, followed by the preparatory course of one year. They will then be divided into combat teams in pairs. Each combat team will be assigned an instructor who will arrange courses for them according to their aptitude.
Training Droids
Special droids used for Androids' combat training with a huge size.
Soldier of Planet Oro
The military force under the command of Decisionmakers. One of Oro's main forces.
Tetra
A gift for Angela from Ruby. Angela takes it with her wherever she is.

texts.title: Day of Enders
texts.summary: On a stormy night under the thunderclouds, Selena meets Obsidia and answers her with a declaration of war.

blocks.x: As the Aspirants continued their long and arduous resistance, Obsidia, a high-ranking commander of The Enders, finally arrived on Planet Dawnbreak to complete her plan. On that stormy night, she had cast young Selena into the mire of humanity with her own hands. With Selena as her pawn and the entire planet as her chessboard, she quietly awaited the results of her experiment.

And now, beneath the thunderclouds, the girl on the rooftop (Selena) bit down on her candy in her mouth. She raised her head, the corners of her lips lifting slightly, and charged toward this fated chessboard.

Obsidia had long been waiting for this. With an almost gentle motion, she raised her hand to touch Selena's face, as though admiring an object she had carved herself. Behind the Ender Overload, bone chains quietly crawled up from the ground, coiling around Selena's ankle as their spikes draw near. The girl simply gripped the pointed tip, tore it apart, then lifted her eyes to meet Obsidia's.
It seemed the answer was clear. This was not submission, but a declaration of war.

Between them lay the full rift between the creator and rebel, the irreconcilable distance between the words "destiny" and "freedom." Obsidia looked at Selena as the piece she had planted with her own hands tightened her grip on her electric blade, smiling at her with a brightness as dangerous as it was brilliant.
She had never intended to win this world. She simply refused to lose herself.
Then let us see where this destruction will lead.

texts.title: The Ten Aspirants
texts.summary: A card for each of the ten, with role, status, personality and a short profile.

blocks.x: Obsidia
Imperatrix Arashi

Obsidia is an ancient high-ranking Ender with the Storm Citadel as her throne and the entire planet as her chessboard. She has witnessed the birth and fall of countless civilizations, yet she has always waited for an answer the Mother Matrix could never give her. The board has been set, and the pieces have already turned against her. To Obsidia, however the game was finally becoming interesting.
Selena
Silverbolt Raiko

Selena has lived at Selrick Academy as a genius to this day. She belongs neither to humanity nor to her own kind, walking between both worlds for the sake of her own freedom. When the shackles of her past began to tighten, Selena resolutely set out on a path of defiance for the sake of freedom!
Guinevere

As the heir to a financial conglomerate, Guinevere rejected the fate arranged for her: taking over the family business and accepting the shackles known as wealth and power. She trained with everything she had and earned the academy's top score, only to be scolded by her father for neglecting her proper path. Then, on the day partners were chosen, Vexana stood up for her. After Vexana went missing, Guinevere remained convinced she was still alive, because the badge carrying their shared belief had never gone out...
Vexana
Twilight Star

Burdened by a heavy past, Vexana had no friends until Guinevere entered her life and formed the strongest combat duo with her. During one mission, Vexana came face-to-face with the Will of the Planet. She was not corrupted. Instead, her final hope erupted from within she would step into the darkness and endure terrible pain, protecting the world for Guinevere in her own way!
Chang'e
Tech Tensai

Though Chang'e is the director of the Science Division, she wears a children's style white lab coat. Small as she is, she holds the wisdom to shake the future. Her parents died in a surprise attack by The Enders. That grief anger became the drive that pushed her to work day and night, eventually becoming Chief Scientist and being put in charge of the core technology that would one day be used to strike back against The Enders.
Lesley
Deadeye Spectre

Lesley lost her left eye protecting her younger brother, and stepped onto the battlefield for revenge. With her extraordinary talent for shooting, she became the Chief Combat Instructor of Selrick Academy. With the prosthetic eye and giant sniper rifle developed by Chang'e, she became the strongest sharpshooter, protecting this planet left scarred by the arrival of The Enders.
Angela
Cyber Cherubin

As the pinnacle of Planet Oro's technology, Angela never had a true childhood from the moment she was born. She never longed for power, yet she was born as the sharpest blade. It was not until the warmth of Planet Dawnbreak showed her another possibility that, from that moment on, this blade began to develop a will of her own.
Ruby
Mecha Maiden

Ruby was the daughter of Planet Oro's ruling class, raised from a young age as their successor. She was perfectly courteous and never said anything more than necessary-but all of it was nothing more than a carefully stitched disguise, hiding the defection plan she had been preparing for a long time. She secretly altered Angela's code, all to leave herself a way out. But she never expected that the innocent soul she awakened place by piece would ultimately become a bond she could no longer let go of.
Fanny
Blade of Kibou

Born into a military family, Fanny chose to delay her enrollment at sixteen to temper herself on real battlefields. She has never thought of hard work as something that needs to be hidden. Though she arrived at Selrick Academy two years after Layla, she broke Layla's undefeated record in her very first assessment. To Fanny, it was no big deal, but Layla saw it differently. But rankings can always wait. Whenever The Enders attack, the two always stand together without needing to say a word.
Layla
Miss Hikari

Born into a family of technologist, Layla is recognized as a genius at Selrick Academy, though behind that genius lie countless secret late night training sessions. She hates letting others see how hard she works, yet more than anyone, she longs to be seen. Fanny took her place at the top, becoming her first true rival. As for whether that makes them friends... Layla still hasn't made up her mind.

texts.title: Fanny
texts.summary: Fanny's profile, how a military family trained her to fight the Enders, and a squad archive of a battle and a late arrival with Layla.

blocks.x: Stories

Fanny was very straightforward and would speak her mind without any pretense since she had grown up with strict military training. Born in a military family, she had a very strong sense of responsibility and had been trained to join the Aspirants from the start. Unlike Layla, Fanny was honest about her hard work in school and never refrained from sharing battle skills and training methods with others.

Fanny had been taught to fight for humans since she was still a child, which was why she abhorred the Enders. She believed it was her duty to create a brand new world for humans that had no place for the Enders, and so she kept training day after day in the hope of slaying the Enders one day. Her seniors felt responsible seeing she already had callused hands at such a young age and regretted forcing such heavy burdens upon a child. But to their surprise, Fanny expressed her sincere gratitude, thanking them for not treating her like a child and for telling her the truth about the world they lived in. The seniors were relieved and pleased at Fanny's thoughtfulness and began putting more effort into her training.

At the age of 16, Fanny requested to experience defense and combat in real battles instead of signing up for the Selrick Academy. In Fanny's mind, she wasn't good enough to go to that elite school, and the fastest way to improve herself is through battles. Even though in the end, Fanny wasn't allowed on the real battlefields, she still learned valuable lessons from those experienced soldiers.

Two years passed, and the talented Fanny had grown to be even more exceptional and successfully enrolled in the Selrick Academy after an entrance exam, becoming classmates with Layla as a transfer student.

But Fanny couldn't understand why Layla seemed so hostile toward her. She only knew she beat the record that Layla had set and won first place at her first exam in school until a friend reminded her. However, in her opinion, their rankings in school were nothing to be concerned about, as her priority was to become strong enough to defeat the Enders one day. So, she paid little attention to Layla's hostility at first, but her indifference further irritated Layla, as she thought she was being looked down on. In the beginning, Fanny would avoid confrontation with Layla when she provoked her, but after a few times, Fanny started to fight back.
Overall, these little interludes didn't really affect Fanny, and when the Enders came to invade human territories, Fanny and Layla chose to fight against them together!

"Mommy, what's that?"

A child's voice cut through the mass of clamoring people. The little girl raised her head and gazed curiously at the "golden deity" before her. The figure lowered its head as its imposing shadow covered the little girl. Some kind of mysterious energy began to converge in its chest, as if it was about to bestow upon the little girl a kind of heavenly miracle.
Whoosh!
With superhuman speed, a purple silhouette surged forth and snatched the girl.
"I'm flying!"
For a moment, the little girl felt the wind rustling beside her, and when she regained her senses, she saw that she was soaring in mid-air.
After a few momentous leaps, Fanny dropped the little girl off at a safe place.
After setting her on the ground, Fanny turned and rushed back, "Cover me!"

"Oh, you can't handle this on your own?" scoffed Layla, standing behind Fanny and regarding her with disdain. Despite her cutting remarks, Layla nevertheless brandished her weapon to dispatch the nearby Enders.
It was a desperate battle, unlike any other.

The protective dome encompassing the Terrinia had slowly torn apart, its pristine surface replaced bit by bit with pieces of battered tiles and gravel. Time and time again, the Aspirants went on the offensive, fighting for a free future. Who knows how many souls departed from this mortal plane and still remain on that battlefield. In the end, however, mankind was victorious.
The process of rebuilding is a long and painful one, especially when it concerns one's spirit.
"Before this, I felt Enders were nothing more than target practice."

Layla's mood was uncommonly morose. The wails and cries for help she had heard during the previous battle wouldn't leave her mind. In the midst of the fighting, she had managed to calm herself, but now, in the aftermath, she couldn't shake this sense of lingering fear.
No one could witness such horror and come out unaffected.
"There is no place for mercy on the battlefield, Layla. I've told you this."
Fanny sighed with exasperation, her heart equally as heavy, "They'll be back. We're not even close to being strong enough..."
"...Damn them!"
Gazing up at what remained of the ravaged city, the two girls made a promise to themselves.
As long as they live, they will destroy the Enders and bring an end to humanity's suffering.
Passion burns deeply within them, a flame that will never be extinguished, and a light that can break through the darkness.

In the time that followed, Layla's provocative tendencies hardly lessened. In fact, they became worse. Meanwhile, Fanny didn't seem to mind in the slightest. The two girls grew up spending their days immersed in ceaseless combat, and the innocent Layla of old gave way to a battle-hardened soldier who could take charge of any situation. Growing up alongside Layla, Fanny couldn't help but feel a sort of burden upon her shoulders: Layla was a loose cannon that she couldn't control.
One day, when Layla was galloping across the school roof frantically attempting to get to class for the umpteenth time, Fanny couldn't take it anymore.
"Get down, Layla! You'll be in detention all day if they find you." Fanny exhorted as she pulled the ambling Layla to the ground and held her down.
"Relax, nobody's going to find me! Besides..." Layla pointed toward the classroom off in the distance, "If anything, I'll be in trouble if I don't hurry to class!"
Fanny sighed with exasperation, and accompanied Layla to the classroom, where they did end up arriving late.
"I told you! They're really going to throw the book at us this time." Layla exclaimed, throwing her hands up.
"But at least we'll be in detention together, hehe!"

texts.title: Layla
texts.summary: Layla's profile, the secret hours of practice behind her proud face, and a squad archive of a battle and a late arrival with Fanny.

blocks.x: Stories

Layla came from a long line of scientists and technologists in Terrinia. The older generation of the family had held dear this talented girl since she was born and seen her as the hope to continue their family glory. With incredible gifts and support from family, the young Layla succeeded in whatever she did and therefore grew up to be confident and proud.

But as she grew older, the courses were no longer as easy as before, and she started to struggle with study especially after she entered the Selrick Academy. It was then she realized it was far from enough to rely on her talent alone. She needed to put more effort into her study but wasn't willing to let others find out about it, so she would always practice alone at the VR Battlefield at lunch break or after midnight. Every time the exam results came out, Layla would pretend to brush it over, saying it wasn't so hard, while others looked at her with admiration, surprise, or envy. She would feel a strong sense of achievement and practice even harder in secret.

But because of Layla's pride, competitiveness, and outstanding performance in school, a lot of her fellow students thought she was hard to talk to and dared not approach her, so Layla had few friends in the Academy, which had always disheartened her. She thought being good at school would make everyone love her and treat her like friends, but it wasn't the case in reality. Layla could only tell herself to cheer up, but deep down, she was still a little kid afraid of loneliness and longing for friends.

Being spoiled at home meant Layla wasn't very concerned about the Academy's rules. She found an abandoned classroom in the school and took it as a secret lab for her personal research. Not only was she doing research on energy, but she was also interested in modifying her school uniform, battle suit, mecha equipment, and other gadgets to make them look aesthetically pleasing to her.

But one day, a transfer student named Fanny beat the undefeatable Layla and was placed first in school, which was completely unacceptable to Layla. So, sometimes she would deliberately provoke Fanny in daily training, who would often get back at Layla for it. In the meantime, Layla worked even harder in training and aimed to take back the first place in the next exam.

When the Enders came, however, Layla didn't seem reluctant to work with Fanny in the fight against them. Actually, their cooperation turned out pretty well, because Layla believed nothing was more important than saving lives from the Enders.

Drip...drip...

Tears fell to the ground, splashing and forming into small rivulets which are promptly trampled upon by a pair of well-tailored boots. A man's voice resonated with a tone that was full of both disappointment and exasperation.
"You are my daughter. To prepare for the future ahead of you, you must be strong and unyielding."
"You cannot allow yourself to be so weak. Do not disappoint me, Ruby."
"...Yes, Father."

Ruby's father fixed his gaze upon her, yet she kept her head lowered and stared off into the distance, at a place where his shadow didn't reach. If she could get out from under this shadow, even if only for a moment...
Every living thing on Oro bent itself to the planet's will, to its ultimate decree: Balance.

Nothing outside of what was proscribed would appear in this place, for the planet's delicate balance must be maintained above all else. Any group that was deemed to pose a potential threat would destroy themselves from the inside rather than undo this great equilibrium. Furthermore, the council, the organization which was truly in control of the entire planet, would never allow any such group to exist. While such measures might seem extreme, it had proven effective in preventing the resurgence of the Enders. It was for this very reason that Oro had been allowed to operate unopposed for thousands of years.
Oro had experienced unprecedented and continuous development; a fact which all its citizens regarded with great pride.
All except Ruby.

Raised to succeed her father from the day she was born, Ruby had undergone the most draconian of upbringings. Her entire life had been laid out for her, a perfect plan from which she was not permitted to deviate in the slightest. She was a bird locked in a cage, dreaming of the sky, and of freedom.
"Must I inherit this absurd planet? I never asked for any of this!"
A branch could only bend so far before it broke, and before long, she began to concoct a daring plan in her mind.
Drip...drip...
For the first time, there was a leap in her chest. Her eyes slowly opened, glittering with a light that couldn't be human. It was a new dawn for her.

Ruby exhaled. The experiment had been a success. She had created the ultimate mecha. Of all the sharpened blades in the special forces of Balance Keepers, this mecha would become the most pointed. She simply had to wait until the time was right...
"From now on, I call you Angela."
"Yes, I'm Angela!"
Angela's effusive and vivacious smile was almost piercing. Ruby lowered her head, and in her head, she chanted to herself, "You belong to me, and no one else."

Angela's training was brutal and trying, yet she never complained. Perhaps such emotional responses did not exist in androids' programming. They only knew how to receive and carry out orders. Angela, however, was different. Unlike the other mechas, she was capable of feeling emotion.
All of this was Ruby's choice, but in time, she came to regret it.
"This is for you."
Ruby took the flowers that Angela was holding.
"A flower? But how did you..."
"You're my friend, so I want to make you happy."
Ruby stared at the flowers dumbfounded, and emotions that had been suppressed her entire life were given life anew, and blossomed within her.
Drip...drip...
Her tears dripped into Angela's palm.
"What is this?" Angela asked with intense curiosity, holding the tears up to examine them.
"Nothing."
Tears streaked down Ruby's cheeks, but she felt nothing.
"Alright, sit tight until I get back!"

Angela flashed that oh-so-familiar smile as she waved at Ruby. She turned to step into the plane along with other the mechas. They were to carry out a mission. Their destination: the faraway planet of Dawnbreak.
"Wait! I...I want you to have this."
Ruby had produced a miniature doll of Angela and handed it to her. She called it Tetra, and it served as a camera showing Angela's every move while she was on Oro.
Now, glancing at the monitor, Ruby could see all too clearly what Angela was taking part in on Planet Dawnbreak: a massacre.

The council had deprived Angela entirely of her ability to think for herself. She had been turned into a thoughtless killing machine. Ruby gazed upon Angela, and it was as if she were looking at a stranger. She could no longer ignore what she was feeling. It was decided.
She would go to Planet Dawnbreak!

"Ruby, what do you want the most?"

"What I want...is to stay in this free land, with you!"

As the days of murder and bloodshed drifted further into the past, Planet Dawnbreak slowly returned to its former tranquility. With their arrival, the Balance Keepers had brought chaos and destruction, and in their absence, peace had flourished. The planet was riddled with the scars of its haunted past, but this was of little consequence; on this place, the people's faith could never be broken, and hope would always prevail.
"Is it just me, or are those two funny in the head?", Layla asked with concern. Beside her lay a damaged mech, which she was repairing.

"Perhaps, but I have faith in them, and in their resolve. It will give them strength and carry them to victory." Fanny stated, then added, "However, should they ever require it, we should be available to lend our assistance."
Layla's eyes widened in excitement, "Wait, are you saying we can have more battles on other planets?"
"That's no fun", said Fanny, pushing Layla's face away.

They had been tossed in a windowless cell, where they awaited their final sentencing. The dank cell had no ventilation of any kind, and was shut off from all sound. Time stood still. But they still had each other.

Angela had trusted her, and how had Ruby repaid her? She had used her to escape from Planet Oro. Never once had she considered Angela's feelings, and now, in these final moments... she had hurt her.

Angela clasped Ruby's hand. That warmth that so uniquely human slowly spread on own hand, with all its metal and wires, and for a moment, it felt as if that warmth was partly hers.
If freedom is what you want...

Outside of the cell, Ruby's father watched them through the security footage. He couldn't remember when he had last seen his daughter smile. As a father, he had been a stern disciplinarian; he knew that more than anyone. He had wanted to prepare her so she could handle the responsibility and pressure that came with being his successor. As time went on, Ruby had slowly gone silent.

How many sleepless nights had he spent wondering if he was doing the right thing? Had he robbed her of her childhood? After a moment's pause, thoughts of his and her responsibility to Planet Oro would quell any lingering doubts. One's duty to Planet Oro was everything.
But now, Ruby could potentially be executed. He couldn't...no, he wouldn't accept such a thing!
An alarm rang out through the secret facility. Ruby and Angela were attempting an escape, but it didn't matter. What mattered was his daughter's life.
The council was asking for a status report.
"All normal", he responded, shutting off the alarm.
If freedom is what you want...

texts.title: Angela
texts.summary: Angela's profile, her story A Miracle, and a squad archive of the escape from Planet Oro with Ruby.

blocks.x: Stories
The world fell into darkness once more.

Angela closed her eyes and felt the electricity course through her. When an android was damaged, its symptoms were quite unlike that of a human body. Instead of blood, the machine would instead begin to emit sparks and electric discharges.
Other than Ruby, these flashes of electricity were the only way Angela could get herself to feel anything.
Ruby. Her creator, and her greatest friend.

Angela represented the pinnacle of technological advancement on Planet Oro, located in the A-20 system. The Decisionmakers were concerned that Angela would instill fear in the people and result in a sort of backlash. They were also afraid that the will of the planet would interfere with their plan. As a result, Angela had been kept in seclusion, hidden from society since the day she was born.

Angela was an android; a bionic mechanism created in the likeness of a human. Her appearance would never change for as long as she lives. Despite never having anything remotely resembling a childhood, her lack of exposure to the outside world left her with the innocence and naivety of a child. She longed to experience and explore the world that lay beyond, but was forbidden from doing so. Instead, she was forced to spend all her days in and around the laboratory. The only person she ever saw that was the same age as her was Ruby, her creator, who was the daughter of one of the Decisionmakers.

While Angela had no inherent interest in such things as physical capabilities, the cutting-edge technology responsible for her creation had imbued her with a formidable strength far beyond anything a human could ever dream of achieving.

With Angela amongst their ranks, Oro's Balance Keepers became unstoppable as they ventured from planet to planet carrying out "balance" operations. It was only during these missions to outside planets that Angela was able to enjoy all-too-brief moments of freedom. Once she returned to Oro, she was immediately ushered back into the laboratory.
Rain, clouds, sunshine...what were the most quotidian of everyday phenomena to most, were objects of a great desire to Angela.
The civil unrest in Planet Dawnbreak caught the attention of those in Oro, and the Decisionmakers dispatched Angela, along with other Balance Keepers to restore balance.

Hovering in the air above Planet Dawnbreak, Angela glanced down at the planet in amazement; it was unlike anything she had ever seen. The city seemed immaculate and to function like clockwork. Its citizens appeared to be enjoying happy, peaceful lives. Any hint of unhappiness was soon wiped away once the sun came out, and the entire city basked in its warmth. These young men and women, who had been designated as their targets, seemed to be doing nothing more than living their lives in a state of serenity, which took Angela aback.
But it was too late. There was a loud, resounding beep, and Angela's cognitive functions disappeared. She was being controlled by the Decisionmakers, as were all the others on her team.
When she came to, Ruby was behind her. Ruby had rushed to Planet Dawnbreak to free Angela from her mind control, and her rage had robbed her of reason.
Ruby had gone out of control, and Angela watched in horror as Ruby lifted her weapon. No, this couldn't be happening.
Ruby may not have said much, but she was always kind to Angela. She would never do something like this!
"Ruby!"

Angela cried out. Perhaps it was Angela's concern for Ruby that helped bring her back to her senses, or perhaps it was a miracle of some kind. Whatever the reason might be, Angela's screams snapped Ruby back to reality.
"You created me. You set me free. I can't let you become the way I used to be. There's only one thing in this world that I know is real, and that's how I feel about you."
From this point on, no more shall we part.

texts.title: Selena: A Storm Born of Rebellion
texts.summary: Selena's earliest memory, her double life as a student and an Ender, and the night she turns on Obsidia's recall.

blocks.x: The scent of mud on that stormy night was her earliest memory of the world.

Draped in an oversized nightgown that had belonged to a human casualty, she stood barefoot on the scorched earth left behind by The Enders' mothership. Around her, human screams mingled with the roar of the downpour.
When Karina, a member of the rescue team, gathered the little girl into her arms, the girl remained expressionless. Yet almost by instinct, she wrapped her arms around Karina's neck...
Why were these carbon-based lifeforms so warm, yet so fragile? Why did that warmth make the Ender cells in her blood cry out for conquest, while also stirring an instinctive desire to cling to it?
In the days that followed, the girl enjoyed Karina's care. To fit in, she learned to mimic how humans smiled and adopted human restraint. She even chose a human name for herself: Selena.
But Selena had always known she was different.
To her, it was all a game of pretend. Destructive power and dangerous thoughts came naturally to her, yet the humans around her only praised them as signs of her unique talent.

Their praise never truly meant anything to her. What fascinated her instead were the cold mecha constructs at Selrick Academy. The circuits and energy coursing through them felt far more like what flowed through her own veins.

Getting into the Science Division was like a children's game to Selena. The professors marveled at her instinctive understanding of the Aspirant mechas, never realizing that she herself was a living source of the technology they studied.

She personally modified a compact mecha suit known as Silverbolt. To everyone else, it was the product of everything she had learned at the Academy, a powerful weapon built to defend the city. They were amazed that Selena alone could operate it so well.
But only Selena knew the truth: Silverbolt was, in every sense, a weapon of The Enders.

Late at night, Selena would slip into the shady areas along the city's outskirts with Silverbolt. Using the storm for cover, she would shed her Academy uniform and allow purple biomechanical tissue to spread across her body. Then she would race through the city like a shadow, free to go wherever she pleased.
She relished the freedom of living between two worlds. She even openly sold Ender technology recovered from wreckage to Vexana, curious to see how another pawn like herself might escape the game.

Her comms were never quiet. Academy assignments, mercenary jobs, black-market deals... Selena took them all on. The sense of controlling her own destiny only fueled her ambition. She loved this freedom, and the feeling that she could bend the world to her will.

She soon discovered just how rewarding that freedom could be. In the human world, it seemed to be a privilege reserved for the most brilliant. With her intelligence and the identities she moved between, Selena could navigate even the most volatile situations and walk away without a scratch.
But a "privilege" built on deception could never withstand the scrutiny of truth.

Selena deliberately ignored the mysterious transmission buried among her messages. She knew exactly what it was: a recall from The Enders, a command etched deep into her cells, and an invisible shackle trying to drag her back to the cold, rigid Mother Matrix.
Obsidia's recall followed her like a shadow. The fearsome huntress was already crossing the sea of stars, closing in on Selena.

To The Enders, Selena had always been a bold experiment placed in the heart of human society. They were willing to let their pawn move freely for a while, granting her a small taste of "freedom." But if she ever slipped beyond their control, there would be only one outcome: termination.
Once Selena realized someone from the Mother Matrix was coming for her, she quickly weighed the choice that best served her survival and interests.
She had no intention of returning to a Mother Matrix ruled by nothing but slaughter and control. Nor did she intend to die protecting humanity.
When Obsidia's hunter descended through the clouds above the Academy, Selena was waiting atop the bell tower in the middle of the storm.
She wore her human uniform and the polite smile she had learned to mimic from humans. A quick glance at the Academy below confirmed the coordinates. She immediately pushed Silverbolt into overload.
She knew that refusing the order to return meant betraying The Enders, and that they would hunt her without end.
But so what?

She would rather live as "Selena," a name she had chosen for herself, than remain someone else's pawn. She wanted to explore on her own terms, take control of her own destiny, and even take the Imperatrix's place if she had to.
"This so-called destiny... it doesn't sound cool at all."
Selena chose neither to flee nor to submit.
Rampant electricity surged through her body, completely transforming her into her combat form. She would use the very signal meant to call her back to trace Obsidia's coordinates instead.
"Sorry, but I still prefer life at the Academy. Still, if you really want me to choose..."
She took a deep breath as arcs of electricity split the clouds above her, opening a path toward The Enders' mothership, the target of her ambitions.
"Even on the path to destruction, I'm taking the scenic route!"
Lightning swallowed her silhouette, and Selena vanished into the clouds.
Below, the city was left in chaos; stunned spectators could only stare as a storm unlike any before raged overhead:
A storm born of rebellion.

texts.title: Obsidia: The Desire for a Different Ending
texts.summary: The first Ender to awaken, her experiment with Selena, and the ending she wants to see.

blocks.x: The scent of mud on that stormy night was Selena's earliest memory of the world. To Obsidia, it was merely another string casually plucked over the course of her long existence.

Obsidia was the first consciousness to awaken among The Enders. From their mindless, perpetual instinct to destroy, she alone carved out a sense of self. While the rest of her kind still fed and killed on biological impulse alone, Obsidia had already learned to observe. She watched stars collapse, civilizations burn to ash, and even witnessed the vast, cold Mother Matrix that brought her into existence.

To humanity, she was a nightmare descending from above the clouds, the mastermind seated aboard the colossal mothership known as the Storm Citadel. She moved with effortless calm and grace, for she had no need to set foot on such an insignificant world herself.

Whenever the dark clouds of the Storm Citadel spread across the land, its magnetic storms brought disaster to humanity in an instant. Amid that deathly violet glow, a slight lift of her finger was enough to command storm and lightning, bringing one effortless massacre after another.
"Destruction is simply the start of a new cycle."
Yet having absolute control brought Obsidia no satisfaction. Instead, it gave rise to a nothingness that followed her like a shadow.

She watched with indifference as her kind were born into slaughter and perished in ever-ending war. In time, she began to ponder a question that even the Mother Matrix could not answer: once Planet Dawnbreak had been reduced to nothing and human civilization had been completely "cleansed," what then?
What fate awaited The Enders when they no longer served a purpose? Would it be an eternal slumber, or an endless cycle of self-annihilation?
Driven by an almost clinical curiosity, Obsidia conducted an experiment many years ago.

During a heavy downpour, she placed a young Ender specimen now known as Selena, the first to possess a perfect human form, into a human settlement. From the edge of the Storm Citadel, she watched with keen interest as the humans took into their arms a seed capable of destroying their entire civilization.

She did not care whether Selena would betray them. She only wanted to see what kind of twisted yet magnificent flower would bloom when an Ender's core is steeped in human warmth, selfishness, and ambition.
Years later, when that child began making a name for herself at Selrick Academy and even tried to resist Obsidia's recall signal, Obsidia was not angered.
If anything, it only made the game more interesting.
Selena's little schemes, her ambition, her absolute hunger for freedom... all of it brought Obsidia a rare flicker of amusement amid the vast nothingness.
The girl thought she was deftly playing at infiltration and betrayal. She thought building the "Silverbolt" mecha suit would give her the leverage she needed to reclaim her freedom.
But to Obsidia, every carefully planned act of defiance was merely a puppet's final dance before the strings tightened.
To make the performance even more entertaining, Obsidia played along, deliberately leaving flaws in her own plans to lead Selena toward the most complete act of "betrayal."

She needed a lieutenant capable of seeing through the game, or perhaps an opponent capable of posing a genuine threat. She wanted to see just how far Selena could go. Only a betrayal powerful enough to shake the board was worthy of becoming an uncertainty in Obsidia's long existence.
But how could a puppet ever act beyond the will of the one pulling its strings?
Selena charged toward the Storm Citadel, streaking through the storm like a bolt of lightning.
Obsidia stood at her throne, her inhuman, mecha-like shell gleaming with a cold sheen amid the crackle of electricity.
She looked down at the girl coming straight for her, the pawn she had placed with her own hands, watched grow, and now saw turning against her.
Obsidia parted her lips. As she studied Selena's face, filled with defiance and an unyielding will, she felt a pleasure she had not known in a very long time.
"Look at how much you've grown, my child."
Her voice remained perfectly calm, but the violet light in her eyes burned with a fervor more intense than ever before.
If Selena could usurp her, or create a third possibility beyond the choices already on the board, then the catastrophe unleashed upon Planet Dawnbreak would finally have meaning.
Obsidia still believed everything was under her control, yet what she truly sought was to see the entire game fall apart at the very end.
She was the Imperatrix of The Enders, the ruthless mastermind.
But her madness ran deeper, a desperate desire to witness "a different ending."

texts.title: The Lonely Champion
texts.summary: Layla, proud and secretly working hard, longs for friends until a transfer student takes first place.

blocks.x: Layla came from a long line of scientists and technologists in Terrinia. The older generation of the family had held dear this talented girl since she was born and seen her as the hope to continue their family glory. With incredible gifts and support from family, the young Layla succeeded in whatever she did and therefore grew up to be confident and proud.

But as she grew older, the courses were no longer as easy as before, and she started to struggle with study especially after she entered Selrick Academy. It was then she realized it was far from enough to rely on her talent alone. She needed to put more effort into her study but wasn't willing to let others find out about it, so she would always practice alone at the VR Battlefield at lunch break or after midnight. Every time the exam results came out, Layla would pretend to brush it over, saying it wasn't so hard, while others looked at her with admiration, surprise, or envy. She would feel a strong sense of achievement and practice even harder in secret.

But because of Layla's pride, competitiveness, and outstanding performance in school, a lot of her fellow students thought she was hard to talk to and dared not to approach her, so Layla had few friends in the Academy, which had always disheartened her. She thought being good at school would make everyone love her and treat her like friends, but it wasn't the case in reality. Layla could only tell herself to cheer up, but deep down, she was still a little kid afraid of loneliness and longing for friends.

Being spoiled at home meant Layla wasn't very concerned about Academy's rules. She found an abandoned classroom in the school and took it as a secret lab for her personal research. Not only was she doing research on energy, but she was also interested in modifying her school uniform, battle suit, mecha equipment, and other gadgets to make them look aesthetically pleasing to her.

But one day, a transfer student named Fanny beat the undefeated Layla and was placed first in school, which was completely unacceptable to Layla. So, sometimes she would deliberately provoke Fanny in daily training, who would often get back at Layla for it. In the meantime, Layla worked even harder in training and aimed to take back the first place in the next exam.

When the Enders came, however, Layla didn't seem reluctant to work with Fanny in the fight against them. Actually, their cooperation turned out pretty well, because Layla believed nothing was more important than saving lives from the Enders.

texts.title: Defending an Undefeated Record
texts.summary: Fanny trains from childhood, enters Selrick Academy as a transfer student and beats the record Layla set.

blocks.x: Fanny was very straightforward and would speak her mind without any pretense since she had grown up with strict military training. Born in a military family, she had a very strong sense of responsibility and had been trained to join the Aspirants from the start. Unlike Layla, Fanny was honest about her hard work in school and never refrained from sharing battle skills and training methods with others.

Fanny had been taught to fight for humans since she was still a child, which was why she abhorred the Enders. She believed it was her duty to create a brand new world for humans that had no place for the Enders, and so she kept training day after day in the hope of slaying the Enders one day. Her seniors felt responsible seeing she already had callused hands at such a young age and regretted forcing such heavy burdens upon a child. But to their surprise, Fanny expressed her sincere gratitude, thanking them for not treating her like a child and for telling her the truth about the world they lived in. The seniors were relieved and pleased at Fanny's thoughtfulness and began putting more effort into her training.

At the age of 16, Fanny requested to experience defense and combat in real battles instead of signing up for the Selrick Academy. In Fanny's mind, she wasn't good enough to go to that elite school, and the fastest way to improve herself is through battles. Even though in the end, Fanny wasn't allowed on the real battlefields, she still learned valuable lessons from those experienced soldiers.

Two years passed, and the talented Fanny had grown to be even more exceptional and successfully enrolled in the Selrick Academy after an entrance exam, becoming classmates with Layla as a transfer student.

But Fanny couldn't understand why Layla seemed so hostile toward her. She only knew she beat the record that Layla had set and won first place at her first exam in school until a friend reminded her. However, in her opinion, their rankings in school were nothing to be concerned about, as her priority was to become strong enough to defeat the Enders one day. So, she paid little attention to Layla's hostility at first, but her indifference further irritated Layla, as she thought she was being looked down on. In the beginning, Fanny would avoid confrontation with Layla when she provoked her, but after a few times, Fanny started to fight back.
Overall, these little interludes didn't really affect Fanny, and when the Enders came to invade human territories, Fanny and Layla chose to fight against them together!

texts.title: We Believe!
texts.summary: The Enders fall from the sky, Selrick Academy is founded, and Layla and Fanny set out to fight them.

blocks.x: The Enders came from the sky, crushing the prosperity of human civilization inch by inch. In the face of their invasion, humanity armed itself with military force and technology.

With the birth of Aspirant mecha suits designed specifically to fight The Enders, Selrick Academy was officially established in Terrinia to recruit young warriors with pure and powerful Aspirant power.

There, two very different girls, Layla and Fanny, met and came to understand each other. Through the moments they shared in training, their beliefs grew even stronger. Holding fast to the belief that "the blade of aspirant power will sever despair," Layla, Fanny and the other young warriors who pilot Aspirant mecha suits bravely set out on their journey to fight The Enders.
Though The Aspirants' struggle to defend humanity has only just begun, they firmly believe that one day, humanity will embrace hope and return to the green fields beneath blue skies.
